headline: South Asia: Pakistan warns India against attempt to alter strategic balance
script:
Good morning. This is your global conflict briefing.

- South Asia: Pakistan warns India against attempt to alter strategic balance.

- Jamaica Gleaner, 9 hours ago: THIRSTY FOR CASH - NWC seeks massive rate hike, warns of investment cuts without it as debts mount.
The Office of Utilities Regulation (OUR) has confirmed that it received an application from the National Water Commission (NWC) for a 51 per cent increase in tariff over a five-year period. The NWC’s senior management told a meeting of the Public Accounts Committee (PAC) at Gordon House on Tuesday that the utility had applied to the regulatory body last Friday, putting its approximately 500,000 customers on notice. In a release yesterday, the OUR said the tariff application covers the period 2026-27 to 2030-31.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: Pakistan warns India against attempt to alter strategic balance.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: Pakistan warns India against attempt to alter strategic balance.
ISLAMABAD: Adviser to the National Command Authority retired Lt Gen Khalid Kidwai on Tuesday warned that Pakistan could review its deployment options to restore strategic balance in South Asia, saying India was moving towards a more prepared, potentially first-use capable nuclear posture. “Pakistan never has and never will accept strategic imbalances to be induced in South Asia,” Mr Kidwai said at the second Islamabad Non-Proliferation Conference, hosted by the Strategic Vision Institute, an Islamabad based think tank specialising in strategic issues.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 6 hours ago: US envoy to meet Putin after 'positive' talks with Zelensky.
Washington’s envoy Steve Witkoff arrived in Saint Petersburg early Wednesday to meet with Russian President Vladimir Putin following what US Secretary of State Marco Rubio described as “positive” talks with President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine. The trip by President Donald Trump’s special envoy is part of efforts to draw a line under a bitter feud between him and Zelensky over the war with Russia. After talks with Witkoff in Oslo, Zelensky thanked Washington on Tuesday for the resumption of US intelligence sharing on Russian strikes.

ISLAMABAD: Iranian leaders have told Pakistan that the United States must take the first steps to rebuild trust, and that the acceptance of Tehran’s seven-point proposal could provide a starting point for renewed negotiations. The message was conveyed during Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir’s visit on Tuesday, where he met with President Masoud Pezeshkian, Parliament Speaker Bagher Ghalibaf, Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Mohsen Rezaei, a representative of Iran’s supreme leader and secretary of the Supreme National Security Council.
India - bottom line: Israel planned intense strikes against Iran on Oct 10, but Trump said no: Report.
- Times of India - Top Stories, Jerusalem Post, just now: Israel planned intense strikes against Iran on Oct 10, but Trump said no: Report.
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu was preparing an aggressive attack on Iranian targets amid growing tensions. However, US President Donald Trump opposed these military actions prior to the midterm elections. Reports indicate that Israeli military forces were ready to launch strikes on October 10, focusing on critical Iranian infrastructure. Diplomatic efforts regarding Iran's nuclear program and US sanctions remain contentious and unresolved.
- Times of India - Top Stories, 3 hours ago: China reveals advanced nuclear subs in Pacific test; a look inside its submarine fleet.
In a significant military advancement, China announced the successful test-firing of a strategic missile by its advanced nuclear submarines in the Pacific Ocean. This milestone underscores the increasing strength of China's underwater naval capabilities aimed at enhancing its military deterrence. While specific details of the missile remain undisclosed, experts suggest that this may signify a pivotal shift in China's undersea nuclear strategy, potentially unsettling US maritime superiority in the Indo-Pacific.

AUSTRALIA
Australia - bottom line: My late wife Jo Cox was murdered in her constituency in 2016. The alleged attack on Helen Haines is a punch to the gut | Brendan Cox.
- The Guardian - Australia, 15 hours ago: My late wife Jo Cox was murdered in her constituency in 2016. The alleged attack on Helen Haines is a punch to the gut | Brendan Cox.
Moments like these can reinforce our divisions or remind us of what we stand to lose when hatred and intimidation are allowed to brutalise our democracy It’s never a good sign when you turn on your phone to find a dozen messages asking if you are OK. For reasons you will come to understand, I only get those messages when something awful has happened. So on Monday, when I came out of an all-day meeting on antisemitism and picked up the messages from friends, I clicked across to check the news with real dread.
- The Guardian - Australia, Jerusalem Post, 5 hours ago: Australian MP Helen Haines attacked with car: what we know so far - The Latest.
A man has been charged after the Australian MP Helen Haines was allegedly attacked with a car outside her electorate office in the state of Victoria. Haines, who is an independent MP, has lost one leg as a result of the incident and surgeons were fighting on Tuesday to save the other leg. Police say 43-year-old Brendan Nugent has been charged with dangerous driving causing serious injury, intentionally causing serious injury and causing harm to a commonwealth public official. Annie Kelly speaks to Guardian Australia political editor Tom McIlroy Continue reading...
- The Guardian - Australia, 11 hours ago: Australian democracy is usually peaceful. But there’s a homegrown history of political violence | Joshua Black and Frank Bongiorno.
Like other features of our public landscape, both good and bad, political violence has a history in Australia – one from which we may learn The alleged attack on independent MP Helen Haines in Wangaratta has shocked a nation whose politics is normally peaceful even by the standards of mature democracies. A hard-working, decent parliamentarian with a strong moral compass and a gift for achieving consensus, Haines seems an especially unlikely figure to attract the kind of brutality allegedly visited on her on Monday. We do not yet know the motivation behind this alleged attack.
